title: Book Three · Chapter 13: Another Page for Leo
story:
Near the end of the third week, Ronan leaves his lunch box open on the desk.

The last piece of egg is under some rice. He finds it and eats it.

Anna is checking a page in her new maths book. Her finger rests beside the last question.

“Do you want to go outside?” he asks.

“In a minute. I want to finish this one.”

“The ball game is near the wall.”

“I will find you.”

Ronan takes his box to the shelf. Then he goes downstairs.

The boy with the ball sees him at once.

“Here!”

Ronan catches the first throw. He sends it across to another boy. This time the ball stays well below the top of the wall.

“The wall is hungry,” someone says.

“It can wait,” Ronan answers.

They spread out. The ball moves faster now. Ronan misses one throw and has to fetch it from beside the tree.

When he comes back, Anna and her friend are on the steps.

“Finished?” he calls.

Anna holds up one thumb.

Her friend points toward the field. The girls go that way together. Ronan turns back to the circle.

At home that evening, he takes his unfinished page from the drawer. He puts Leo's letter beside it.

He reads the question about Anna and the track. Then he begins his answer.

Dear Leo,

Anna still runs faster. She runs with her friend too. I can run one whole lap now. I run at my own speed.

She likes maths questions. Some of them look like windows. You count the squares. I can show you one next time.

He leaves some space and draws the square with nine small squares inside it.

Count all the squares. Don't stop at nine.

Then he writes about the ball game. He tells Leo about the wall and the fish on the board.

At the bottom, he adds two questions.

Does the man still put the red box out first? What does the shop sell?

Mum comes to the table with a short piece of thread on her shoulder.

Ronan points to it. She looks down at the wrong shoulder.

“Other side.”

She finds it and drops it into her work basket.

“Another letter?”

“Yes. I want to send it tomorrow.”

“I have a customer in the morning.”

“I can go. I know the way now.”

“All right.”

Ronan signs his name. He puts the page aside until the ink is dry. Then he opens Leo's letter once more and looks at the large shoe.

He has not drawn a bun in his answer. He adds one beside the square. Half of it is missing.

Dad looks over his shoulder.

“Where is the other half?”

“Still warm. I had to eat it.”

Dad laughs and goes to wash his hands.

Ronan folds the new letter. Tomorrow he can take it to the post office. Tonight he puts it on his shelf and joins Mum in the kitchen.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

spread out＝分散站开；fetch＝去取回；hold up＝举起；sign one's name＝签上自己的名字。

## 理解问题

1. Anna这天为什么先留在教室？后来她和谁去了操场？
2. Ronan在第二封信里向Leo分享了哪些新生活？这封信在本章结束时有没有寄出？

## 读句子

**He puts Leo's letter beside it.**

拆开看：He / puts Leo's letter / beside it.

他／把Leo的信放下／放在它旁边（it指尚未写完的信纸）。
